It uses a finite state machine and counters to generate the necessary timing signals and pixel data. The design is implemented in Verilog and is intended for educational purposes. results.summary: This project receives sound level data from an INMP441 microphone and runs sound recognition on it. It displays the recognized note on a 7-segment display of a TM1638-based interface module. It also draws color patterns on a VGA screen using the Tiny VGA interface. The design is written in SystemVerilog and was prepared as a test for the Verilog Meetup variant of the Tiny Tapeout Verilog Project Template.

results.summary_before: This project implements a 4-channel PWM generator with programmable frequency, duty cycle, and phase offset for channels 2-4. It uses an 8-bit input bus to load control registers, with a 7-segment display showing the current register address, and outputs PWM signals on four bidirectional pins. The design is built using the Wokwi simulator and is intended for educational purposes. It has been tested on fabricated silicon.
results.summary: This project celebrates a marriage covenant by displaying the letters JONANDANgIE on a seven-segment display. It has two modes of operation: dip switches can drive a single letter state, or a button can be used as a clock to cycle through the letters in order. It is built using the Wokwi simulator. The design is intended to be tested by pressing the clock button and reading the seven-segment display.

results.summary: This design uses two configurable gates to drive SR and D flip-flops, enabling a variety of complex flip-flop functions. It is built with the Wokwi simulator. When SEL and INV are low, the 0 inputs directly drive the flip-flops, and A-0 can be connected to the clock for use with the D flip-flop. The outputs include multiplexer and XOR results as well as the flip-flop Q and Q# signals.
